figures.caption: Figure 1: Overall workflow of the proposed EEG-driven decoding framework. Stage 1 summarizes the simulator experimental settings and the dataset. Stage 2 shows the EEG preprocessing and analysis of cognitive insights. Stage 3 presents RSL: hazardousness is defined on Risky/Not Risky and Dangerous/Not Dangerous axes to form three valid levels (Safe, Low-Risk, High-Risk) and corresponding labels for RP and DI. Stage 4 illustrates model construction, including the PCM and PEDS, and the resulting RP and DI. Dashed boxes indicate the decoded auxiliary signal for downstream AV actions, i.e., alarms and executions, shown for context but not studied in this work.

Figure 2: Overview of the experimental setting and dataset composition. The figure includes the driving simulator and EEG acquisition environment, participant demographic distributions (gender, age group, and driving experience), and the composition of the simulated traffic events used in the experiment.
Table 1: Details of traffic events, including ID, Target Type, Action, Direction (Dir.), Distance (Dist.), and Risk Level.

Figure 4: Visualization of EEG topographic maps aligned with traffic scenarios over a unified timeline. The middle section illustrates two driving scenarios: a high-risk cut-in event (Event 8; top) and a low-risk cut-in event (Event 6; bottom). The passenger vigilance zone is color-coded, with green indicating safety and yellow-to-red representing increasing perceived risk. The surrounding EEG topographic maps depict neural activity at different time points, using two temporal resolutions: 50 ms (detailed neural dynamics) and 400 ms (general activation patterns). Warmer colors (red) indicate increased brain activity, and cooler colors (blue) denote lower neural activation.

Figure 5: The Passenger Cognitive Model (PCM) illustrates “Calm” and “Nervous” mental states according to surrounding traffic scenarios and topographic plots and summarizes the overall cognitive process.
Figure 6: Peak Latency Analysis of Channels “Fz” and “PO3” under Event 1 (top left), Event 2 (bottom left), Event 3 (top right), and Event 4 (bottom right).

Figure 7: Architecture of the proposed 3D-CRNN. The input EEG is first segmented into a causal pre-onset window for RP and an event-centered window for DI. Each branch reshapes the EEG into an electrode topology-informed 3D representation and extracts features through local spatial convolution, temporal convolution/pooling, and global convolution. The branch features are then concatenated and modeled by a GRU layer with 32 hidden units for final classification. Blue denotes the RP branch and purple denotes the DI branch.
